purpose: Cevimeline is used to treat dry mouth in people who have Sjogren's syndrome, an autoimmune condition that damages the glands that make saliva. It helps your mouth produce more saliva so eating, speaking, and swallowing feel more comfortable. It can make a big difference in your day-to-day quality of life.
how_it_works: Your saliva glands have special switches called muscarinic receptors. Cevimeline works by turning on those switches, which tells your saliva glands to produce more saliva. Think of it like pressing a button that tells your body to make more moisture in your mouth.
common_side_effects: The most common side effects include sweating, nausea, runny nose, diarrhea, and flushing (feeling warm or red in the face). You may also notice increased urination or watery eyes. These happen because the medication activates similar glands throughout your body, not just in your mouth.
warnings: Do not take this medication if you have uncontrolled asthma, narrow-angle glaucoma, or iritis (eye inflammation), as it can make these conditions worse. Tell your doctor if you have heart disease, kidney problems, or gallstones before starting this medicine. Avoid activities requiring sharp vision at night, as it can affect how your eyes adjust to low light. Call your doctor right away if you have trouble breathing, chest pain, or vision changes.
typical_dosing: The usual dose is 30 mg taken three times a day by mouth. It can be taken with or without food, but taking it with food may help reduce stomach upset. Try to space your doses evenly throughout the day, such as morning, afternoon, and evening.
